record.name: South Sudan
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified; few sources are available. A June 2025 report records officials calling for AI legislation and digital infrastructure.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. The retrieved material does not sufficiently establish the national AI governance arrangements. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

Re-ran searches in English for a government-designated institute that evaluates advanced models, or a commitment, proposal or study naming one. No qualifying institute or commitment was identified; results described ministry statements on AI infrastructure and skills, summit participation and the Cybersecurity and Computer Misuse Bill. Kept low: ministry pages record AI ambitions and summit participation but do not show a national AI governance set-up. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

searches.query: South Sudan AI safety institute government
South Sudan government artificial intelligence policy strategy ministry ICT 2026 AI safety institute

check.language_note: English is an official language or an official language of national administration; it is a practical national search language for this check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Some submitted strings contain site. rather than site:; these literal strings are preserved and are not treated as domain-restricted searches. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. Preserved result batches, using 1-based positions in check.searches: SS-search = searches 1, 2 (en, en). Each multi-query batch has only a combined returned result set; its source_ids cannot be attributed to individual queries. Historical query dates are recorded as 17 October 2026 in the phase6 search-boundary ledger. On 24 October 2026 the record was searched again in English; the result links of each query were matched against registered sources in the same way.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.

related_bodies.name: Ministry of Information, Communication Technology and Postal Services
related_bodies.role: Officials have spoken about AI; no policy or evaluation body was found.

record.notes:
A UNESCO project page on an AI roadmap for ICT policy returned an access error and was not read.

The June 2025 Eye Radio account reports officials' calls for an AI legislative framework. A separate official-domain search returned unrelated institutes and an external governance index; no second substantive official national AI-governance source was retrieved. English-language searches for a government-designated AI safety institute with a remit to evaluate advanced models included a separate search of gov.ss.

next_check.reason: Routine re-check on a two-year rotation of states with no reported plans.
